implementation_notes: Jackson, the dominant JSON library, implements the pattern declaratively: @JsonTypeInfo(use = Id.NAME, include = As.PROPERTY, property = "type") on the base type plus @JsonSubTypes entries supplies the tag vocabulary, and the mapper's polymorphic deserializer instantiates the mapped subtype - the subtype map is the allow-list. The JDK's own mechanism, ObjectOutputStream writing the class name and serialVersionUID into the stream and ObjectInputStream resolving it, is the format-introduced variant of the same idea but a legacy path: enable it only behind an ObjectInputFilter allow-list and never for untrusted payloads. Sealed interfaces make the subtype set a compile-time fact, which pairs well with @JsonSubTypes but does not by itself validate the tag.
pitfalls: Enabling default typing (activateDefaultTyping/enableDefaultTyping) or Id.CLASS lets the payload name the class it wants instantiated; the Jackson project's own CVE criteria and OWASP both treat that as the unsafe-deserialization entry point - use Id.NAME with an explicit subtype allow-list instead.

Id.DEDUCTION removes the tag and picks the subtype from which fields are present: that is inference, not the pattern, and it mis-binds once additive evolution makes two subtypes distinguishable by the same field.

On the JDK path, ObjectInputStream reconstructs whatever the stream names, so an ObjectInputFilter allow-list is mandatory, and serialVersionUID drift turns a harmless class edit into a failed read of every stored payload.
